# Submitting Your Lens

## Introducing Lens Folders[​**](#introducing-lens-folders "Copy to clipboard")

We are introducing Lens Folders to manage all Lenses for you and your teams. With this evolution, you will be able to create Lens Folders to manage and distribute Lenses for yourself, as well as for your teams and organizations.

### What are Lens Folders?[​**](#what-are-lens-folders "Copy to clipboard")

Lens Folders are the home for your Lenses. With Lens Folders, you can organize your Lenses based on your needs, and share access to the Lens Folder with members of your teams and organizations. With Lens Folders, a Lens can be created independently of where it will be used. If you are working with a business or an advertiser, your Lens can be assigned to another profile other than yourself, as well to multiple ad accounts, provided that they are in the same organization.

#### For existing My Lenses users[​**](#for-existing-my-lenses-users "Copy to clipboard")

Snap will automatically create an Organization and a Lens Folder for all your current Community Lenses. Those Lenses will automatically be distributed to your profile with no interruptions. Your historical Lens metrics and visibility setting will not be impacted.

You will also be able to create a new organization and a new Lens Folder during the submission flow.

#### For new Lens Creators[​**](#for-new-lens-creators "Copy to clipboard")

You will be able to create a new organization and a new Lens Folder during the submission flow.

## Project Set Up[​**](#project-set-up "Copy to clipboard")

Before submitting your Lens, make sure you have configured your project info. For more information about configuring your project info, please refer to the [Configuring Project Info](/lens-studio/publishing/configuring/configuring-project-info.md) guide. Next, make sure your Lens meets the performance requirements detailed in the [Performance and Optimization](/lens-studio/publishing/optimization/overview.md) guide. Finally, make sure the Lens you are submitting meets our [Submission Guidelines](/lens-studio/publishing/submitting/submission-guidelines.md).

To submit, select the `Publish` button in the top right corner of Lens Studio. This opens the `My Lenses` window. If you have not configured your project info, the project info window will be opened instead.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

### Log Into Snapchat[​**](#log-into-snapchat "Copy to clipboard")

You'll now be prompted to log into Snapchat. The username and password are the same ones you use for your Snapchat account.

![](/assets/images/submitting-your-lens_login-1-5ee9cd573df8e208546bb9e569149b06.png)

Next, you'll be prompted to authorize Lens Studio. Click `Continue`.

![](/img/lens-studio/5-publishing/submitting-2.png)

Once authorized, close the window and go back to Lens Studio.

![](/img/lens-studio/5-publishing/submitting-3.png)

## Set up an organization and a Lens Folder[​**](#set-up-an-organization-and-a-lens-folder "Copy to clipboard")

You need to set up an organization to create a Lens Folder. If you do not yet have an organization, you will be asked to create a new organization in the submission flow.

![](/assets/images/lens-folder-1-03cb926f6647e6610487feb5d6452ed5.png)

You can select an existing organization if you already have one, and set up a Lens Folder under your selected organization.

![](/assets/images/lens-folder-2-3816abc68b0efc9457642c18054fb38d.png)

### Select a Lens Folder[​**](#select-a-lens-folder "Copy to clipboard")

Once you have set up your Lens Folder, you can select the Lens Folder to submit your Lens. You can set up multiple Lens Folders under one organization to manage the permission and access of your Lenses.

![](/assets/images/lens-folder-3-dbd4c173935a8b7c59dc1f3474f9e706.png)

### Submit as a new Lens or Update an existing Lens[​**](#submit-as-a-new-lens-or-update-an-existing-lens "Copy to clipboard")

You can either submit the Lens as a new Lens, or update an existing Lens under your selected Lens Folder.

### Adjust Lens Details[​**](#adjust-lens-details "Copy to clipboard")

After a Lens Folder has been selected, you’ll be prompted to add information on your Lens. Here you can add Tags to help Snapchatters find your Lens, and Scan Triggers.

To learn more about adding tags to your lens, see the [Snap AR Tags of the Month](#snapar-tags-of-the-month)section.

### Upload to Lens Folder[​**](#upload-to-lens-folder "Copy to clipboard")

If you are not ready to publish your Lens to Snapchat yet, choose the Upload to Lens Folder option. The Lenses will not be published anywhere and you will be able to update the Lens from your Lens Folders.

If you are a Camera Kit partner and do not wish to distribute your Camera Kit Lens to the Snapchat app, you should select Upload to Lens Folder. Then, the Lens will only be uploaded to your Lens Folder and will be available in your Camera Kit Lens Scheduler.

If you are a Lens Creator who works with a business organization, and want to publish your Lens to a Profile or an Ad Account that belongs to another organization, you should select Upload to Lens Folder. The Lens then will only be uploaded to your organization’s Lens Folder and will be available in Business Manager for distribution.

### Upload and Publish[​**](#upload-and-publish "Copy to clipboard")

If you are ready to publish your Lens to Snapchat and let Snapchatters to view and use your Lens, choose “Upload and Publish”. You will be able to modify the Lens Visibility later.

Only choose “Upload and Publish” if you want to publish the Lens to the logged in user’s account.

![](/assets/images/lens-folder-publishing-lens-b07e83d2b1183d52a3b18c877212b128.png)

If you wish to publish the Lens to your own profile, choose “Upload and Publish”. You can also set the Visibility of your Lens.

Finally, click Submit Lens to submit your Lens.

Before submitting your Lens, we recommend creating a preview video. If you have added your preview video in the Project Info window, you do not need to add another one here. For more information on creating a preview video, follow the [Creating a Preview Video](https://developers.snap.com/lens-studio/references/guides/publishing/configuring/creating-a-preview-video) guide.

When you're done you will be presented a with a congratulation message where you can head to My Lenses where you can manage the new Lens, as well as all the Lenses you've already submitted.

## My Lenses[​**](#my-lenses "Copy to clipboard")

Once you've uploaded your Lens, you'll be taken to the My Lenses portal. Here, you can see all Lenses that you've uploaded and monitor the submission process. You can also get to the My Lenses portal directly by pressing the `My Lenses` button in the top right of your Lens Studio project window.

![](/assets/images/submitting-your-lens_myLenses-7c443372ac6af62a1336ee2be8b7d84b.png)

Here you can search for your Lenses, get its status, change its details, as well as get its Snapcodes or Link so you can share it.

You will see all Lenses on your personal profile on the “All Lenses” tab.

### Organization Drop Down[​**](#organization-drop-down "Copy to clipboard")

If you want to look for Lenses in a specific organization / Lens Folder, you can open the organization drop. Here, you will find a list of organizations that you have access to.

![](/assets/images/lens-folders-org-dropdown-d765dd8a870931e158b20c5b4e26c073.png)

![](/assets/images/lens-folder-org-dropdown-large-2afd8db80d9ee82495ac6fac860077d2.png)

When you land on an organization, you can switch between different Lens Folders using the filter.

Snap has introduced a search bar in the Organization dropdown that allows you to search My Lenses by Organization ID, Org Name, Lens Folder ID, Lens Folder Name, Ad Account ID, Ad Account Name, Business Profile ID, or Business Profile Name.

### Manage Members (Only for users who work with business)[​**](#manage-members-only-for-users-who-work-with-business "Copy to clipboard")

If you want to manage members for your organization / Lens Folder, click on Manage Members button. You will be taken to Snap’s [Business Manager](https://business.snapchat.com/) to manage members for your organization and Lens Folders.

#### Roles and Permissions of Lens Folders[​**](#roles-and-permissions-of-lens-folders "Copy to clipboard")

Members in your organization can have one of three roles on a Lens Folder:

| Roles             | Permission                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Lens Folder Admin | Lens Folder Admins can view, create, manage, and delete Lenses within a Lens Folder, as well as manage and delete the Lens Folder itself.                                                                           |
| Lens Manager      | Lens Managers can view, create, and manage existing Lenses in a Lens Folder. They cannot take action on the Lens Folder itself.                                                                                     |
| Lens Creator      | Lens Creators can only view existing Lenses and create new Lenses in a Lens Folder that are not made available to the Snapchat community. They cannot take any other action on the Lens Folder or Lenses within it. |

Organization Admins have full access to Lens Folders. Business Admins can view all Lens Folders and assign roles to others and themselves. Learn more about [roles and permissions here](https://businesshelp.snapchat.com/s/article/roles-permissions?language=en_US).

### Lens Folder Deletion[​**](#lens-folder-deletion "Copy to clipboard")

Lens Folders belong to Organizations, and therefore can’t be deleted. You can, however, [delete your Lenses](https://developers.snap.com/lens-studio/references/guides/publishing/submitting/lens-visibility-settings#delete) from the Lens Folder.

If you delete your Snapchat account, Lenses in your Lens Folders will not be deleted. If you DO NOT want your Lenses to be used in Snapchat, please make sure that you delete all your Lenses before deleting your account.

## Lens Statuses[​**](#lens-statuses "Copy to clipboard")

Below you will find a brief description for each state your Lens could be in. Your Lens' current status is displayed in the `Status` column of the `My Lenses` portal.

### In Review[​**](#in-review "Copy to clipboard")

While the Lens is waiting to be approved, the Lens will show as `In Review` under `Status`. If this is the first time you've submitted this Lens you won't yet have a Snapcode or any Lens stats.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

### Live[​**](#live "Copy to clipboard")

Lenses that are live will show as `Live` under `Status`.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

You can get a link to the Lens by clicking on the link icon on the right side next to the `...` button. Additionally, you can download the Snapcodes for the lens by click on the `...` icon, and selecting `Download Snapcode`,

![](data:image/png;base64,)

For best practices when sharing, please refer to the [Sharing Your Lens](/lens-studio/publishing/distributing/sharing-your-lens.md) guide.

### Offline[​**](#offline "Copy to clipboard")

Sometimes you may want to take a Lens offline. To do this, click on the Lens, and under Visibility, choose `Offline`.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

While a Lens is offline, the Snapcode will be deactivated and anybody who scans it will be shown an error message.

![](/assets/images/submitting-your-lens_set-offline-098653d630a899b1cd8dd3498c676d41.png)

At any time, you can make it `Live` again by changing its visibility.

When deactivating (or reactivating) a Lens it can sometimes take approximately 10 minutes before the Snapcode stops working.

### Invalid[​**](#invalid "Copy to clipboard")

Sometimes there might be a technical issue with your Lens.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

If this is the case, the status of your Lens will show as `Invalid`. There will be one or more reasons shown to help you debug and fix your Lens. You can then submit an update. Please refer to the [Submission Guidelines](/lens-studio/publishing/submitting/submission-guidelines.md) under "Technical Requirements" for some reasons why it may be invalid.

![](/assets/images/submitting-your-lens_invalid-reason-d98bf79e124aee037256c947f331b166.png)

If the Lens has already been Live and it's just your most recent submission that is `Invalid,` the previous version will remain active and it can still be used by Snapchatters.

### Rejected[​**](#rejected "Copy to clipboard")

If the Lens has been rejected, the Lens will show `Rejected` under `Status`.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

For more information on why a Lens might have been rejected, please refer to the [Submission Guidelines](/lens-studio/publishing/submitting/submission-guidelines.md). When your Lens is rejected, it can no longer be unlocked.

![](/assets/images/submitting-your-lens_rejected-reason-6eca404b7e78103d5a504d72f8f1e16e.png)

However, if your Lens has been rejected you have the opportunity to modify your Lens Project, fix the content, and submit an update.

## Lens Submission Error Reporting[​**](#lens-submission-error-reporting "Copy to clipboard")

In general, all Lens submissions go through a 3-step process before they are published to Snapchat. The **Validation** step is the first to happen within the process. Before Lenses are submitted for further testing, Lens metadata is read to ensure the Lens being submitted meets certain requirements, such as the version of the Lens package being submitted. Once the validation step is passed, Lenses are pushed to the **Automated Testing** stage which is where the bulk of Lens testing occurs. Lenses are checked for performance, device compatibility as well as memory usage across an array of devices (iOS and Android). The final step includes **Content Review**. In the Content Review step, all Lenses are reviewed to ensure they do not contain any assets or attachments that violate Snapchat’s [Community Guidelines](/lens-studio/publishing/submitting/submission-guidelines.md#lens-content-requirements).

There may be cases in which you run into technical issues during the **Validation**, **Automated Testing,** or **Content Review** phases of the Lens submission process and your Lens may be rejected. To find more details about the rejection, you can find the Lens within the ‘All Lenses’ view of My Lenses and click on the Lens name to learn in which stage of the Lens submission process it failed.

![image alt text](/assets/images/lens-error-reporting-0-3e50942f364e1fcb402bf83428464368.png)

![image alt text](/assets/images/lens-error-reporting-1-76863d92e64b77d54c19b7d39f166197.png)

If a Lens fails in any part of the submission process, My Lenses shows you which step the issue occurred. By clicking on ‘Error Logs’, a modal will pop up and you will be able to see more details on the specific failure:

![image alt text](/assets/images/lens-error-reporting-2-25727ef9d61e7ba7472f8f39df80a0f7.png)

If these occur, please use the [Lens Troubleshooting guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lBZ_ypVgUWtpgFu_37s0BTUgi3_PXVEmZbthk1xLFdE/edit#heading=h.4ak3i3zdb8xi) and follow the steps to locally test your Lens within Lens Studio.

## Lens ID[​**](#lens-id "Copy to clipboard")

Each Lens has a unique identifier. This is useful for being able to distinguish different Lenses you have submitted if they have a similar name or icon. It will also be needed for possible support requests.

To copy your Lens ID go to My Lenses and select the Lens you need the ID from. Click on the copy icon and your Lens ID will be copied to your clipboard.

![](/assets/images/submitting-your-lens_lens-id-37da0b683b8fd04d886863463cff5321.png)

## Snap AR Tags of the Month[​**](#snap-ar-tags-of-the-month "Copy to clipboard")

Tags of the Month is a way for Lens Creators to get exclusive access to the predicted hottest Lens topics of the month. Tags are sourced from both on-platform and off-platform repositories to highlight the “hottest” themes/trends of the moment and are meant to serve as a source of inspiration as you build Lenses. Using tags is a great way to get noticed on Snapchat because we love featuring high quality Lenses that are creative and use trending tags!

### Applying Tags of the Month to your Lenses[​**](#applying-tags-of-the-month-to-your-lenses "Copy to clipboard")

1. On the Lens Studio homepage, you will see the "Tags of the Month" section. You can hover over the tag to get inspiration on the type of Lens what to build.

   ![](/assets/images/trending_homepage-f62007d369aee16ed17befe96449dcff.png)

2. Clicking on the Tag automatically applies it to the next project you open.

3. Tags that you have clicked will be automatically applied through the Lens submission process. This means that you do not have to remember to select them again when you submit your Lens.

4. When you are in My Lenses, you will also see the “Tags of the Month” section.

   ![](/assets/images/tagsofthemonth-749a33207a2f8296aa2b69f306f49325.png)

5. If you did not do so in Step (2), you can click on the tags that are relevant to your Lens here. They will be automatically applied to the “Lens Tags” for your Lens.

6. Please be aware that the expiration date is typically a few days before the actual event or holiday.

Please only add Tags of the Month to Lenses where they are directly relevant to the topic. Tags are moderated and irrelevant tags will not help you gain more distribution on Snapchat.

### Here are some tips to create high quality Lenses:[​**](#here-are-some-tips-to-create-high-quality-lenses "Copy to clipboard")

Please follow the steps below to ensure your lens qualifies for maximum distribution on Snapchat:

1. No copies of ML or viral Lenses.
2. [No default Lens Studio icons](/lens-studio/publishing/submitting/submission-guidelines.md).
3. Interesting & clear Lens previews.
4. Add Lens Hints which will help Snapchatters understand how to use your Lens.
5. Try to optimize/compress the resources in your Lens. A smaller Lens size (i.e., less than 8MB) is better. See the [optimization guide](/lens-studio/publishing/optimization/performance-optimization-guide.md) for more information.
6. Try to avoid “Subscribe to me” text in the Lens. Users will probably create less content with the Lens, and there is a chance that your Lens will not achieve maximum distribution on Snapchat.
7. And finally – use our Tags of the Month when you submit your Lens!

## Lens CTAs[​**](#lens-ctas "Copy to clipboard")

Members of our Snap Lens Network (SLN) also have access to the Lens Call-to-Action (CTA) feature, which allows you to include web links directly in your Lenses!

When you are onboarded to the SLN, you will see the feature appear as the following within My Lenses:

![](/assets/images/lenscta_mylenses-3941942c6f343875a2776806b7a869a9.png)

This feature allows SLN members building in Lens Studio to include a web URL or an app deep link that appears as a CTA attachment overlaid on the Lens. Inclusion of the URL/deep link to your Lens occurs both at the Lens Submission phase in Lens Studio or can be edited or added later through My Lenses.

You will be able to add a Website URL or an app deep link to drive traffic to your website or app.

![](/assets/images/LensCTA_3-b91b2dbf8d76a5bfdbe085e7a93c766f.png)

The CTA must relate to the content in your Lens. If it does not, the CTA may be subject to removal.
